deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a programmatic outline of an axiomatic, Euclid-free (absolute-geometry) theory of parallels in the sense of Lobachevsky and Bolyai. The red 'VIII' marks material printed in Gauss, Werke VIII ('Parallelismus'). The notation ab* means the ray from a through b, prolonged indefinitely.

(1) DEFINITION. Ray ab* is parallel to ray cd* if three conditions hold:
(i) they are coplanar;
(ii) they do not meet;
(iii) every ray af* issuing from a into the open region *bacd* meets cd*. That region is bounded by ray ab*, segment ac and ray cd*.
This is the 'limiting' (asymptotic) parallel: ab* is the first non-cutting ray in the pencil at a.

(2) Parallelism does not depend on the initial point c of cd*. No proof is given. [Mine: if c is replaced by another point c' of the line cd, the regions differ by a bounded triangle. A ray from a that crosses that triangle must leave it through the side on line cd, by Pasch's axiom.]

(3) Parallelism does not depend on the initial point a of ab*.
Case I, a' on ray ab*: a ray a'f* inside the region; [mine] the ray af through a point f of it meets cd* in g by hypothesis. Then a'f* enters the region bounded by af, g, c, a' and must leave it through cg.
Case II, a' outside ab* (a between a' and b, per the figure): take a'f'* inside region b a' c d. Construct af* with angle baf = ba'f'. Equal corresponding angles mean af and a'f' cannot meet (exterior-angle theorem). Hence af* lies inside region bacd, so it meets cd* in g. The ray a'f'* enters the region a'agc. Since it cannot cut af*, i.e. segment ag, by Pasch it must cut cg.

(4) SYMMETRY: if 1 is parallel to 2 (ab* to cd*), then 2 is parallel to 1.
- By (3), take a = the foot of the perpendicular from c to line 1 (ca perpendicular to 1).
- Suppose 2 is not parallel to 1. Then some ray from c inside angle acd misses 1. Let cd' be the ray from c parallel to 1 [existence of the limiting ray assumed, a continuity argument]. Then 0 < acd' < acd; put delta = dcd'.
- Take b on 1 on the side of the parallels with acb = delta/2. Take b' on the other side with acb' = acb, so that cb = cb' and triangle cbb' is isosceles.
- At b, draw be on the side towards 2 with angle cbe = angle cb'b. This angle is a base angle, so it is < 90 deg < angle cb(1). Hence be lies in the region of the parallel b1 to cd* (independence of starting point), and so meets cd* at e'.
- Mark g on 1 beyond b' with b'g = be'. By SAS (cb' = cb, angle cb'g = angle cbe', b'g = be'), triangles cb'g and cbe' are congruent, so angle b'cg = angle bce'.
- In angles measured from ca, with theta = acd and theta' = acd': angle bce' = theta - delta/2, while angle b'cg = acg + delta/2. Hence acg = theta - delta = theta'.
- So cg makes the same angle with cb' as cd', i.e. cg = cd'. But cg meets 1 at g and cd' does not. Absurd.

(5) TRANSITIVITY (stated only): if 1 is parallel to 2 and 1 to 3, then 2 is parallel to 3.

(6) Definition of corresponding points on two parallels. [Known from Werke VIII: the segment joining them makes equal angles with the two parallels.]

(7) A point on a third parallel corresponding to a point on the first also corresponds to the corresponding point on the second (transitivity of correspondence).

(8) Arrangement (order) of corresponding points. The marginal numerals 8/7 indicate that items 7 and 8 were to be swapped; a struck line '8. Die Grenze ist die L...' was abandoned.

(9) 'Grenze': the limit curve, i.e. the locus of points corresponding to a given point in a pencil of parallels (horocycle; in space the horosphere).
errors: Prop. 4: choosing b on line 1 with angle acb exactly = delta/2 requires delta/2 < acd'; otherwise the ray at that angle does not meet line 1. This is a minor gap. It is easily repaired: any angle acb = alpha with 0 < alpha <= delta/2 and alpha < acd' gives acg = theta - 2*alpha >= theta'. That contradicts the fact that cg meets 1 (which requires acg < theta').
Prop. 4 tacitly uses the existence of the limiting parallel cd' from c, which needs a continuity (Dedekind-type) argument, and uses Prop. 3 (moving the vertex to b) without saying so.
Prop. 3, case II tacitly uses that rays with equal corresponding angles do not meet (exterior angle theorem, valid in absolute geometry) and Pasch's axiom. Case I is only sketched.
Props. 2 and 5-9 are stated without proof (an outline).

results.what: Definition of (asymptotic/limiting) parallel rays via the 'first non-cutting ray' condition
results.usually_credited_to: Lobachevsky (1829/1840), J. Bolyai (1832); Gauss's notes published in Werke VIII (1900)

results.what: Independence of parallelism from the starting points of the rays
results.modern_name: Parallelism is a property of rays (ends), not of initial points
results.usually_credited_to: Lobachevsky, Bolyai; Gauss (letter to Schumacher 1831, Werke VIII)

results.what: Symmetry of asymptotic parallelism, proved by an isosceles-triangle/SAS contradiction
results.usually_credited_to: Bolyai (Appendix §2), Lobachevsky; Gauss in Werke VIII

results.what: Transitivity of parallelism; corresponding points; limit curve ('Grenze')
results.usually_credited_to: Bolyai (L-line), Lobachevsky (horocycle); Gauss's notes Werke VIII

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's known outline 'Parallelismus' (c. 1831), printed in Werke VIII (the red 'VIII' marks it as published). The content is foundational non-Euclidean parallel theory long credited jointly to Gauss, Bolyai and Lobachevsky.

checkable.sympy: theta, theta1 = symbols('theta theta1', positive=True); delta = theta - theta1; alpha = delta/2; simplify((theta - alpha) - alpha - theta1) == 0
checkable.asserts: From angle b'cg = angle bce' with acb = acb' = delta/2, the angle acg = theta - 2*alpha equals acd' = theta1 (core of Prop. 4).

checkable.sympy: theta, theta1, alpha = symbols('theta theta1 alpha', positive=True); simplify((theta - 2*alpha - theta1).subs(alpha, (theta-theta1)/2 - Symbol('eps', positive=True)))
checkable.asserts: For alpha < delta/2, acg = theta - 2*alpha exceeds theta1 by 2*eps > 0 (repair of the gap: any small alpha still gives a contradiction).
Model check (hyperbolic plane, curvature -1): the angle of parallelism Pi(x) satisfies sin Pi(x) = 1/cosh x, a well-defined limiting angle as in Prop. 1.

transcription_corrections: Line in 3.II: the image reads roughly 'so wird a'f' [struck word] die af* nicht schneiden, also cg', i.e. a'f' cannot cut af*, therefore it cuts cg. It does not read 'entweder die af* oder [?] schneiden'.
In 3.I, 'Es sei ist auch' is probably a false start, best read as 'Es ist auch a'b* parallel mit cd*, wenn a' auf ab* liegt'.
The struck line reads '8. Die Grenze ist die L...' (abandoned). The marginal numerals '8' and '7' indicate interchanging items 7 and 8.
The label at upper left of figure 2 is b' (left of a), consistent with b' being the mirror image of b in the perpendicular ca.
